model: Broker-dealer FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net debt zero, retention on common equity

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 6.6% diverges >30% from EPS 5yr CAGR 19.7% and net revenue 3yr CAGR 17.5%: the EPS/revenue CAGRs run from a cyclical trough (FY23 ROE 3.1%, EPS JPY30.86) to a cyclical peak (FY26 ROE 10.1%) and must not be extrapolated. Book growth is the conservative anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue = net revenue (RevenuesNetOfInterestExpense) FY21 1,401.9 / FY23 1,335.6 / FY26 2,167.7 JPYbn; EPS basic JPY50.11 / 30.86 / 123.08; equity = NHI shareholders' equity 2,694.9 / 3,148.6 / 3,707.9. FCF CAGRs are null: OCF-based FCF for a broker-dealer is dominated by trading-book and collateral movements (FY22 -974bn, FY26 -1,197bn on record profit) and is not an owner-FCF series. SBC grew 28.3bn (FY21) -> 40.8bn (FY26), 7.6%/yr, slower than net revenue (9.1%), so SBC is not eating the reported growth.

scenario_narratives.base: Nomura's FY3/26 ROE of 10.1% (record attributable profit JPY362bn) and Q1 FY3/27's annualised 15.4% are partly structural and partly cyclical. Structural: Wealth Management's 17 straight quarters of net inflows into recurring, AUM-based fees as Japanese households move savings into NISA accounts; Investment Management enlarged by the Macquarie public asset-management acquisition (AUM ~US$770bn, 35%+ outside Japan); a reformed Wholesale cost base. Cyclical: strong equity markets, record Equities revenue (+41% YoY in Q1) and FICC activity, which management already says slowed into H2. The base case books a strong FY3/27 (+10% net revenue, ROE ~12%) then lets ROE settle near 9.7% -- just above the 9.5% JPY cost of equity and below the raised 10-12%+ Vision 2030 target -- so the business is worth about book plus a modest premium for growth.
scenario_narratives.bull: Vision 2030 is delivered and held: Japan's savings-to-investment shift proves durable and Nomura captures it through wealth inflows and the enlarged asset manager scaling on a fixed platform, while Wholesale earns through the cycle without a repeat of the Archegos (FY3/21) or FY3/19 international losses. ROE stays ~11.5-12% and pre-tax income passes the JPY750bn target by FY3/30, with terminal growth 2.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The market cycle turns after a strong first half: Japanese equity turnover and international trading fall back toward FY3/23 conditions (ROE 3.1%), net revenue drops 10% then 2% in FY3/28-29, and margins compress to 18-20%. A risk-management loss of the Archegos kind, Macquarie-integration disappointment (goodwill JPY172.5bn), or another conduct case like the 2024-25 JGB-futures spoofing matter adds to the drag. ROE settles at ~6.5%, well below the cost of equity, and the stock is worth materially less than book.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Nomura is valued as a financial institution: free cash flow to equity (profit to common less the retention needed to grow book) discounted at a JPY cost of equity, with net debt zero because the balance sheet's liabilities are operating funding. The question the model answers is whether today's ~1.2x book is earned by a sustainable ~10% ROE or capitalises a cyclical peak.
key_risks_to_valuation: Peak-cycle base: FY26 ROE 10.1% and Q1 FY27 15.4% annualised versus a ~7% FY17-26 average; the base case still assumes ~9.7% through the cycle.
Trading and risk-management losses (Archegos FY3/21 ~USD2.9bn; FY3/19 loss year) are lumpy and not captured in smooth paths.
Regulatory/conduct risk: the 2024-25 JGB-futures manipulation case and the employee robbery scandal hit Japanese retail franchise and corporate bond underwriting.
JPY/USD: the ADS value moves 1:1 with the yen; a stronger yen lifts USD value with no change in the business.
No filing text extracted; the Q1 FY3/27 figures come from NMR_Analysis.json, not a parsed 6-K, and the balance sheet anchor is 2026-03-31.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 6.71-10.94. Tokyo 8604.T and JPY=X from the same API for the parity check.
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 0001163653), Form 20-F FY3/26 (year ended 2026-03-31): net revenue, pre-tax income, tax, NI attributable and NCI, NHI shareholders' equity, goodwill, SBC, dividends paid, buybacks, shares outstanding, weighted basic/diluted shares; research/NMR/Reports/NMR_Metrics.csv and kpis (equity-award taxes, cash taxes).
data_sources.qualitative: research/NMR/Reports/NMR_Analysis.json (2026-10-04: Q1 FY3/27 results, Vision 2030 targets, H2 commentary, CET1) and research/NMR/info.json.

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted, 1 ADS = 1 ordinary share. 2,901.34m ordinary shares outstanding ex-treasury at 2026-03-31 (20-F FY3/26 cover; 3,088.56m issued after 75m cancelled in FY26) plus 98.9m dilutive share-based awards (20-F EPS note: weighted diluted 3,041.2m less weighted basic 2,942.3m) = 3,000.2m. Held FLAT: SBC (plus equity-award withholding taxes) is expensed in the flows, and buybacks (JPY101.5bn FY26) are the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat, so they are a use of the FCFE being valued, not extra value. Nomura is a funded repurchaser (JPY59-102bn/yr FY24-26).
inputs.sbc_source: 20-F FY3/26 XBRL: ShareBasedCompensation JPY40,836m (cash-flow add-back) plus equity-award withholding taxes on net-share settlement JPY18,214m (kpis equity_award_taxes FY2026); no combined company figure is published, so the two lines are summed per house policy = JPY59,050m, 2.72% of net revenue. The GAAP SBC is already inside US GAAP pre-tax income; the margin path adds it back and the engine re-charges the full 2.72%, so the house basis carries ~JPY18bn/yr pre-tax more cost than GAAP.
inputs.fcf_definition: Broker-dealer FCFE basis, not owner FCF. Reported OCF/FCF is meaningless for a securities firm (trading assets, repos and collateral swing OCF by trillions: FY26 OCF -JPY843bn on record profit), so the FY0 fields are earnings-based: reported_fcf = FY3/26 net income attributable to NHI shareholders JPY362,129m + GAAP SBC add-back JPY40,836m = JPY402,965m (street cash earnings); last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes JPY59,050m - interest_income 0 = JPY343,915m (house earnings to common, before retention). Interest income is the broker's revenue, not excess-cash income, so it is not stripped. Memo: FY3/26 distributions actually paid = dividends JPY179,742m + buybacks JPY101,499m = JPY281,241m (78% of attributable NI). Forward FCFE in the engine = profit to common less the equity retention required to grow book in line with the business.
inputs.fx_note: fx_rate converts JPY (model) to USD (quote): 1/157.83 = 0.0063359, Yahoo Finance JPY=X 157.83 at 2026-10-03T21:07Z. 1 NMR ADS = 1 ordinary share, so JPY per share = JPY per ADS; the *_jpy twins are JPY per share. Parity check: Tokyo 8604.T close JPY1,507 on 2026-10-02 / 157.83 = US$9.55 vs the NYSE NMR close at price_as_of (ADR ~1.9% above local, consistent with the later US close and the 1:1 ratio; a wrong ratio or direction would be off by orders of magnitude).
inputs.fy0: FY2026 (year ended 2026-03-31; Nomura calls it FY2025/26)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Single JPY cost of equity 9.5% across all scenarios (risk charged once, via scenario weights and paths). Built in the flows' own currency: JGB 10-year ~2.0-2.3% (assumption, not fetched) + beta ~1.25 to TOPIX (a broker-dealer's earnings are more market-sensitive than a megabank's; MFG was valued at 9.0%) x Japan ERP ~5.5-6.0% = ~9.0-9.8%. A USD-built rate would overcharge JPY flows by the rate differential.
inputs.lease_treatment: Financial institution: rent/occupancy sits inside non-interest expense, i.e. inside pre-tax profit. lease_cost_pct_path = 0, no lease liability in the bridge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, inside the flow: the margin is calibrated to pre-tax profit less NCI (FY26 NI to NCI JPY12.3bn, mostly consolidated funds/VIEs), so modelled FY0 profit ties to attributable NI JPY362bn. No NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.data_quality_warning: Metrics.csv labels every period USD but values are JPY millions (XBRL hardcoded-USD bug, same class as MFG/HDB/BILI). CSV Revenue is GROSS revenue including interest and dividend income (FY26 JPY4,758bn); the economic top line is net revenue (RevenuesNetOfInterestExpense, JPY2,168bn), which is what base_revenue uses. CSV NetIncome is ProfitLoss incl. NCI (374.4bn); attributable is 362.1bn. CSV FreeCashFlow is OCF-capex and meaningless for a broker. No filings extracted (Extracted/ is empty). Guidance-year judgment uses NMR_Analysis.json (2026-10-04): Q1 FY3/27 annualised ROE 15.4%, raised Vision 2030 targets (ROE 10-12%+, pre-tax >JPY750bn), H2 slowdown commentary, CET1 ~13.1%. The Q1 FY3/27 6-K balance sheet was not extracted, so book and share count stay at 2026-03-31 (the ~JPY60bn of buybacks completed by mid-April 2026 are FY26 cash already in buyback_cash; no new programme committed).
inputs.notes: MODEL: broker-dealer/investment bank -> dcf-methods routing row 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker' (residual income on book, run as FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine -- the house precedent for financials: MFG, HDB, IBN, HSBC, BMO, USB, WFC). No prior NMR valuation and no MEMORY.md entry. Engine mapping: revenue = net revenue (gross revenue less interest expense); 'ebitda' = pre-tax profit attributable to NHI before SBC (FY26: 539.8 pre-tax - 12.3 NCI + 40.8 SBC = 568.4bn = 26.2% of net revenue; FY25 26.6%; FY24 ~19%; FY17-24 average ~18-20%); sbc_pct = SBC incl. equity-award taxes; da_pct 0 (depreciation JPY68bn is already inside pre-tax profit; IT/premises capex treated as maintenance funded within it); cash tax 28% (FY26 GAAP effective 30.6%, FY25 26.4%; cash taxes paid 22% FY26 and 20% FY25; Japan statutory ~30.6%); 'capex' = equity retention = prior-year common book x that year's growth, expressed as % of that year's net revenue, opening book JPY3,707.9bn (US GAAP NHI shareholders' equity 2026-03-31, incl. JPY172.5bn goodwill from the Macquarie US/European public asset-management acquisition closed in FY26), floored at zero (no capital release modelled in a downturn). Net debt 0: repos, customer payables and long-term borrowings are operating funding of the securities book. Modelled FY0 profit = 2,167.7 x (26.2% - 2.72%) x 72% = JPY366bn vs reported attributable JPY362bn. Implied ROE paths: base 11.9% (FY3/27) -> 9.7%, bull 12.9% -> ~11.4%, bear 9.5% -> 5.6% -> 6.5%, against a 10-year history of 3.1-10.1% (FY17-26 average ~7%). Price ~1.20x book (BVPS ~JPY1,278 basic) and ~12.5x FY26 EPS.

bear.rationale: FY3/27 is partly banked (strong Q1) but H2 turns: net revenue +2% (all acquisition) with ROE 9.5%; then a FY3/23-style downturn -- revenue -10% and -2%, margins 18% -- and ROE settles at 6.5%, the FY17-24 band. Retention floored at zero in the down years and in Y1 (acquisition-only growth); no capital release modelled.

base.growth_rates_rationale: FY3/27 (guidance year) +10%: Q1 FY3/27 delivered an annualised ROE of 15.4% with record pre-tax income in all three divisions (Analysis.json), plus the first full year of the Macquarie US/European public asset-management business (~US$180bn AUM, closed Dec-2025, roughly 3pp of the growth); management flagged Wholesale revenue 'slowed somewhat' into H2 and higher H2 volatility, so the year is not annualised from Q1. Then decelerating to Japan nominal growth (2%).
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: Pre-tax-pre-SBC margin attributable: 28.5% in FY3/27 (implied ROE 11.9%, i.e. a strong Q1 at 15.4% and a softer H2), easing to 25% from FY3/31 (ROE ~9.7%, just above the 9.5% cost of equity). Through-cycle, not peak: management's raised Vision 2030 targets (ROE 10-12%+, pre-tax >JPY750bn) are NOT reached in base -- base pre-tax runs JPY600-680bn -- because the FY17-26 ROE average is ~7% and the targets assume no downturn; the base credits the recurring-fee mix shift with ~3pp of ROE over that history.
base.capex_rationale: Equity retention, not capex: prior-year common book x that year's growth / that year's net revenue; book opens at JPY3,707.9bn and grows only by retention, so terminal retention = book x terminal growth. Y1 retention is on 5% organic growth only (book x 5% = JPY185bn): the acquisition-driven part of FY3/27 growth was paid for in FY3/26 and already sits in opening book (JPY172.5bn goodwill).
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 9.5%/2.0% = 13.6x terminal FCFE, below the 15x cap, so Gordon governs.

bull.rationale: Vision 2030 delivered: implied ROE 12.9% in FY3/27 then ~11.5-12% sustained (inside management's raised 10-12%+ target), pre-tax income reaching ~JPY780bn by FY3/30 (target >JPY750bn). Y1 retention on 9% organic growth (12% less ~3pp acquisition annualisation).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because the valuation starts at peak-cycle earnings (Q1 FY3/27 ROE 15.4%) for a market-sensitive broker-dealer whose ROE averaged ~7% over FY17-26 and fell to 3% as recently as FY3/23, and management itself warns of H2 volatility. Base 50% because the recurring-fee mix shift is real but unproven through a downturn. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs ROE inside the raised 10-12%+ target sustained for a decade, which Nomura has not achieved since before 2008.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
